title: Risk and Audit Committee Effectiveness
summary: An eight-module programme helping risk and audit committee chairs and members oversee risk, control and assurance and report credibly to the board.
intro: This training programme equips risk and audit committee chairs and members to oversee the firm's risk, control and assurance arrangements, challenge the control functions and auditors, and report credibly to the board.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give committee chairs and members a practical understanding of how effective risk and audit committees work and the tools to oversee risk management, compliance, internal audit and external audit. Participants leave able to sharpen their committee's mandate and agenda, challenge the control functions and auditors, and evidence effective oversight to the board and supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: Committee mandates and composition, risk appetite frameworks, overseeing the chief risk officer, compliance and internal audit, external audit and financial reporting judgements, assurance mapping, reading risk MI, chairing the committee, reporting to the board and committee evaluation.
Intended Audience: Chairs and members of board risk and audit committees
Non-executive and independent directors preparing to join a risk or audit committee
Heads of risk, compliance and internal audit, and company secretaries supporting committees
Learning Objectives: Explain the distinct mandates of the risk and audit committees and how they interact
Evaluate the firm's risk appetite framework and its use in decision-making
Oversee the chief risk officer, compliance and internal audit, including their independence and resourcing
Challenge external audit and significant financial reporting judgements
Use assurance mapping and risk MI to identify gaps in oversight
Assess committee effectiveness and agree an improvement plan
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of committee briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies and a committee question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the committee's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No accounting or audit qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
Basel Committee, The Internal Audit Function in Banks (2012)
Institute of Internal Auditors, Global Internal Audit Standards (2024)

modules.title: Committee Mandates, Composition and Interaction
modules.summary: What risk and audit committees are for, how their terms of reference divide responsibilities, and how they work with each other and the board to avoid gaps and duplication.
objectives: Explain the purpose and core responsibilities of each committee
Evaluate terms of reference, membership and independence
Identify overlaps and gaps between committees and the board
syllabus: Supervisory and international expectations, including BCBS corporate governance principles
Terms of reference: what to include and what to leave to the board
Composition, independence, skills and cross-membership
Joint sessions and managing the boundary between risk and audit

modules.title: Risk Appetite Frameworks
modules.summary: How the risk committee shapes and monitors the firm's risk appetite, and how to tell a framework that drives decisions from one that sits on a shelf.
objectives: Assess the risk appetite statement, limits and escalation triggers
Evaluate how risk appetite is cascaded and used in business decisions
Challenge breaches, limit changes and management's response
syllabus: Elements of a risk appetite framework: statement, metrics, limits and triggers
Linking risk appetite to strategy, capital, liquidity and business planning
Emerging and non-financial risks in the framework
Handling breaches and requests to change limits

modules.title: Overseeing the CRO, Compliance and Internal Audit
modules.summary: How committees ensure the control functions have the independence, standing and resources to provide effective challenge and assurance, and how they get the most from their heads.
objectives: Evaluate the independence, resourcing and reporting lines of the control functions
Assess risk, compliance and internal audit plans and their coverage
Identify warning signs of weak or captured control functions
syllabus: The chief risk officer's role, access and protection from dismissal
Compliance monitoring plans, findings and regulatory relationships
Internal audit charter, risk-based plan, quality and follow-up
Private sessions, appraisal and appointment of function heads

modules.title: External Audit and Financial Reporting Judgements
modules.summary: The audit committee's oversight of financial reporting and the external auditor, focusing on significant accounting judgements, audit quality and auditor independence.
objectives: Challenge significant accounting judgements and estimates
Assess audit quality, auditor independence and non-audit services
Evaluate the auditor's findings, management letters and management's response
syllabus: Significant judgements: provisions, valuations, impairment and going concern
Audit planning, materiality and key audit matters
Auditor independence, tenure, tendering and non-audit services
Whistleblowing, fraud risk and internal controls over financial reporting

modules.title: Assurance Mapping and the Three Lines
modules.summary: How committees build a joined-up view of where assurance comes from across the three lines of defence and external providers, and where it is missing or duplicated.
objectives: Explain the three lines model and its limitations
Use an assurance map to identify gaps and overlaps
Challenge reliance on first-line self-assessment
syllabus: The three lines model in practice
Building and using an assurance map
Combined assurance across risk, compliance, internal and external audit
Recognising comfort without evidence

modules.title: Reading Risk MI
modules.summary: The information committees need to oversee risk and control, how to read risk reports and dashboards critically, and how to reshape committee packs so that the key messages stand out.
objectives: Specify the management information and indicators the committee needs
Interpret risk reports, trends and forward-looking indicators
Specify improvements to committee papers and dashboards
syllabus: The core committee information set: profile, appetite, incidents and actions
Key risk indicators, trends and emerging risk horizon scanning
Overdue actions, repeat findings and risk acceptances
Good committee papers: clear asks, balanced views and exception reporting

modules.title: Chairing the Committee and Reporting to the Board
modules.summary: How committee chairs set the agenda, run meetings that produce real challenge and give the board a clear, candid account of what the committee has found.
objectives: Apply good practice in committee agenda setting and chairing
Encourage challenge from members and candour from management
Report committee conclusions and escalations to the board effectively
syllabus: Annual cycle of business and agenda prioritisation
Chairing for challenge: drawing out members and managing dominant voices
Relationships with function heads, auditors and the authority
Committee reports to the board: what, how and when to escalate

modules.title: Committee Evaluation and Improvement
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a committee improvement plan, covering self-assessment, external review, skills, succession and learning from failures.
objectives: Evaluate committee effectiveness using structured self-assessment
Use a skills matrix to plan membership, succession and development
Produce a committee improvement plan
syllabus: Committee self-assessment and external review
Skills, induction and succession for committee chairs and members
Lessons from control and audit failures
Workshop: the committee's twelve-month improvement plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.
